title: Dealer high on cocaine at time of police tussle
article: Mladen Cujko had five times the lethal limit of cocaine in his body when he died on the Trans-Canada Highway during a struggle with an RCMP officer, a coroner's inquest was told Wednesday.

Forensic pathologist Dr. Laurel Gray testified that Cujko died of a cardiac arrest brought on by a very high level of cocaine in his blood. Gray, who performed an autopsy on Cujko at Royal Jubilee Hospital, also found evidence that he had smoked crack cocaine.
The inquest into the death of Cujko, a 33-year-old known drug user from Burnaby, is mandatory because he died in police custody.

The Western Communities courtroom was empty except for a few police officers and witnesses, unlike last year's inquest into the death of Anthany Dawson, which was marked by demonstrations, press conferences and a strong family presence.
Dawson died in August 1999 died after running in and out of traffic and struggling with police.

In her opening statement, coroner Lisa Lapointe told the five- man jury that Cujko was picked up at 9:18 p.m. on Aug. 21 by West Shore RCMP after callers reported that a distraught man was running in and out of traffic at the intersection of Jacklin Road and Goldstream Avenue.
Police originally intended to take Cujko to the Royal Jubilee Hospital, but on the way there he became agitated and started kicking out the windows of the police car, she said.

The officer pulled over the car on the highway and radioed that he intended to pepper spray the agitated man. Somehow, he became involved in a struggle with Cujko. Another officer arrived and the two managed to handcuff Cujko. At that point, they noticed he had stopped breathing. He was pronounced dead at Victoria General Hospital.

Because the inquest will examine the issue of police use of force, coroner's counsel Kenn Kardish asked Gray to describe what she found during the autopsy. The pathologist testified that she found no fractures, no evidence that Cujko had been struck by a weapon, no bruising of the neck structures and no burst blood vessels on the face to suggest any kind of force. Gray said she did not find any fresh puncture wounds or needle marks.
"His behaviour sounds like it would be a state of agitated delirium related to cocaine intoxication," Gray told the coroner.
The jury also heard testimony about Cujko's last hours from Tammy Keleher, a former escort worker, and her common-law spouse Samuel Noel Jackson, a tree-topper and excavator operator.

Keleher said Cujko was a former client who had told her previously that he was expecting a drug shipment from Vancouver and would be trafficking in cocaine. But when Cujko showed up unexpectedly at her house on Aug. 21, acting irritated and fidgety, she asked him to leave.
"It was inappropriate for him to come to the house with the children there," she said.
Jackson said he was angry when he came home from work and found Cujko outside the house.
"He's a freak, a drug-dealing scoundrel that tries giving drugs for sexual favours," said Jackson. He told the jury he overheard Cujko say he wanted to do cocaine with them.
Jackson, standing up and using a white tissue to demonstrate, showed the jury how Cujko put a baggie filled with white powder in his shorts.
"He was taking it down into the crotch area of his pants. It was definitely drugs."
After being told to leave, Cujko jumped in his car and sped away. He was frantic, said Jackson, and drove through intersections without stopping.
Cujko finally pulled into the Co-op Gas Station on Goldstream Avenue. Jackson, who had followed, tried to calm him down.
"He started screaming. He said I stabbed him with a needle. I told the attendant to phone 911. He'd had too much blow."
Cujko kept running around, dodging imaginary assailants.
"The shadows were attacking him," said Jackson. "Shadow monsters were everywhere -- from the left, right, front back. He was going mental."
Jackson went home when two police cars pulled up.
"The last thing I saw he was attacking the police," said Jackson.

The jury also watched a surveillance video taken at the Co-op Gas Bar that night. Cujko circles the car and opens the trunk of his car several times. At one point, he enters the store and holds the door closed so no one else can come in.
The inquest continues today with police testimony.
